item.title: Re-advertisement: Chief Health, P-5, FT, #00082605, Aden, Yemen - MENAR

item.title: National coordinator on teacher/principal appraisal in schools/preschools, Education Section, 1 year 11,6 months, Tashkent, Uzbekistan (Nationals only) Home based with travel
item.description: The Government of Uzbekistan is advancing education reforms to support competency-based education (CBE) and improve learning outcomes. Through the Smart-ED Project for Improving the Quality and Efficiency of Education Services, UNICEF, in partnership with national counterparts, is supporting efforts to strengthen systems for evaluating and developing teachers and school leaders across preschool and general secondary education, including the introduction of performance appraisal mechanisms. Uzbekistan has established professional standards, teacher attestation, and school leader certification systems, providing a strong foundation for accountability, career progression, and professional growth. As reforms continue, there is an opportunity to further strengthen these systems to better support the competencies required for effective teaching and leadership in a CBE environment. International experience shows that effective teacher quality systems combine periodic attestation with continuous performance appraisal that provides regular feedback, mentoring, and professional development opportunities. Building on ongoing reforms, this assignment will strengthen the existing teacher attestation system and develop a performance appraisal framework for teachers and school leaders aligned with professional standards, competency-based education, and the national education quality assurance framework. The assignment will also develop practical tools, guidelines, and capacity-building resources to support implementation and promote continuous professional growth, school improvement, and better learning outcomes.

item.description: Are you willing to support the operational effectiveness and its ability to deliver on the strategic mandate by ensuring efficient, responsive and fit-for-purpose operational services? The incumbent will contribute to a well-governed, efficient and fit-for-purpose Operations function that enables OSE teams to focus on their substantive mandate and supports OSE in delivering high-quality strategy, evidence and knowledge in support of UNICEF’s results for children.

item.title: Education Specialist (Learning and Skills Assessment), P-4, #00133267, Fixed Term Position, Global Programme Division - Education CoE, Nairobi
item.description: Are you passionate about shaping how learning and skills are measured to improve education systems worldwide? Join UNICEF's Global Programme Division Centre of Excellence in Nairobi and help drive evidence-based education reforms that improve learning and skills outcomes for children and adolescents. As Education Specialist (Learning and Skills Assessment), you will provide strategic technical assistance to governments, UNICEF Country and Regional Offices, and partners to strengthen national assessment systems, learning measurement, and tracer studies, with a focus on transferable, digital and green skills, and secondary education outcomes. Working at the intersection of education policy, system strengthening, data, financing and innovation, you will contribute to UNICEF's Every Child Learns Education Strategy 2019-2030 and support countries in building more equitable, resilient and responsive education systems that prepare young people for life, work and active citizenship.

item.title: Programme Specialist - Livelihoods for Adolescent Girls and Young Women (P-3), Temporary Appointment, 364 days, #00138954, Global Programme Division, Generation Unlimited, Bangkok, Thailand (Fully Remote)
item.description: Join Generation Unlimited (GenU) and contribute to expanding economic opportunities for adolescent girls and young women. item.title: Supporter Content – Knowledge Management Intern, Division of Private Fundraising and Partnerships (PFP)
item.description:
UNICEF works in some of the world’s toughest places, to reach the world’s most disadvantaged children. To save their lives. To defend their rights. To help them fulfill their potential. Across 190 countries and territories, we work for every child, everywhere, every day, to build a better world for everyone. And we never give up.
UNICEF’s Division of Private Fundraising and Partnerships (PFP) has ambitious goals to deliver on income and influence. Donor engagement is an important driver of income. The Supporter Content team delivers content from emergency responses, donor stewardship content and virtual & immersive experiences (live, interactive, and compelling, where we use digital technologies to bring to life the work UNICEF is doing in emergency and non-emergency contexts). To support national committees and fundraisersthere are internal SharePoint sites for emergency fundraising support, High Value Stewardship services and a VIRTUAL and Immersive experiences ‘hub’ for fundraisers to preview, and self-serve, everything from invitations to global events, to films and VR experiences to tips and tricks guidance for staging their own Virtual and Immersive experiences. Linked to these is UNICEF’s Data Asset Management system called WeShare which houses and makes available all the content for usersto access and use in their fundraising efforts.

item.title: Project Officer (Data Platform Owner), P-2, Temporary Position, 5 months, Supply Division, Copenhagen, Denmark, #00138951
item.description: UNICEF Supply Division (SD) works to ensure equitable and inclusive access to essential supplies and services for children and their families, in development, humanitarian and fragile contexts. These supplies are critical to saving lives, supporting children’s health and education, and protecting them from abuse, exploitation, and neglect. As the UN’s largest end to end supply chain entity, UNICEF leverages its global reach, market influence, supply chain expertise and partnerships with governments, civil society, private sector, industry, and other stakeholders to meet children’s needs and protect their rights around the world. SD focuses on three result areas to maximize impact, scale, and effectiveness: strategic procurement; supply preparedness and response in humanitarian and fragile contexts; and supply chain optimization. To facilitate and accelerate progress toward these results, SD employs three change strategies: financing for supply and services, supply chain digitalization and supply chain localization.

item.title: Supply & Logistics Manager, P-4, Fixed Term Position, Kabul, Afghanistan, #00132370

The supply chain operations include planning, procurement, contracting, customs clearance, warehousing, in-country transport and distribution, as well as monitoring of supplies, services and construction works. The incumbent collaborates closely with programmes in defining supply interventions to meet programmatic needs and achieve results for children, and provides technical and advisory support to governments, national systems and partners on supply chain management.

item.title: Assistant Representative, P-4, Male, Maldives, FT, #137954

item.title: Business Analyst (Partnerships Effectiveness, Knowledge & Learning), P-2, Temporary Position (364 days), PPR, Office of the Global Director, New York, #00139004

item.title: Senior Adviser WASH (Sanitation) (P-5), Fixed Term, #00133992, Global Programme Division, WASH, Nairobi - Kenya.
item.description: Join UNICEF’s Global WASH Practice and help accelerate access to safely managed, climate-resilient sanitation services for children and communities worldwide. Based in Nairobi, you will provide strategic leadership and technical assistance to governments and UNICEF Country Offices, driving sanitation system strengthening, sector financing, policy reform, innovation, and equitable service delivery. You will lead global efforts across sanitation, WASH in Schools, and Menstrual Health and Hygiene, while supporting climate resilience, governance reforms, digital solutions, and resource mobilization. Working with partners across development and humanitarian settings, you will help shape policies, strengthen institutions, mobilize investments, and scale sustainable solutions that improve outcomes for the most vulnerable children and families. This is a unique opportunity to influence global WASH priorities and contribute to UNICEF’s mission of leaving no child behind

item.title: Digital Impact Officer (Technology for Development), P-2, FT, #00018757, Digital Impact Division, Digital Empowerment – DCOE, Nairobi, Kenya.
item.description: This position supports UNICEF's digital transformation agenda by strengthening country-level access to digital, data, and AI solutions through the TeamOne collaboration model. The incumbent will help coordinate and facilitate cross-country support, contribute to the implementation and quality assurance of digital solutions using the UNICEF Digital Playbook, and ensure alignment with digital standards, cybersecurity, data protection, interoperability, and governance requirements. The role also supports the identification and triaging of country office digital, data, and AI needs, leveraging data and insights to improve support mechanisms and community engagement. In addition, the incumbent will contribute to knowledge management, learning, and capacity-building initiatives, foster knowledge sharing across UNICEF's digital community, and help strengthen digital capabilities across country offices through collaboration, learning events, and community management activities. This position is ideal for candidates with an interest in digital development, knowledge management, AI and data-driven innovation, stakeholder coordination, and digital capacity building in an international development context.

item.description: Join UNICEF's Global Programme Division as a Health Specialist (Adolescent Health) and play a pivotal role in advancing adolescent health and well-being worldwide. Based in Nairobi within UNICEF's Centre of Excellence, you will provide strategic leadership and technical expertise to strengthen adolescent-responsive health systems and services, influence global policy and guidance, and support countries in designing and scaling evidence-based programmes. Working closely with governments, development partners, UNICEF Regional and Country Offices, you will drive innovation, capacity development, knowledge generation, partnerships, and resource mobilization to improve equitable access to quality health services for adolescents and contribute to sustainable results at global, regional and country levels.

item.title: Programme Specialist, P-3, Temporary Position, Majuro, Republic of Marshall Islands, #00138682, 364 days
item.description: Join UNICEF as a Programme Specialist, P-3 in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), and play a pivotal role in advancing children’s rights and development across the North Pacific. This exciting position offers the opportunity to lead and manage high-impact programmes, working closely with government counterparts, development partners, communities, and civil society organizations to deliver sustainable and result-driven solutions for children and families. Ideal for a dynamic professional with strong programme management, partnership-building, and policy engagement experience, the role provides a unique platform to influence development priorities, strengthen national capacities, and support evidence-based programming. As part of UNICEF’s Pacific Multi-Country Office, you will contribute to programme planning, implementation, monitoring, and advocacy efforts while gaining valuable experience in a culturally rich and diverse island context.

item.title: Deputy Representative Operations, (P-5) Fixed Term #86195, Niamey, Niger, WCAR
item.description: An exciting and rewarding opportunity has arisen at the UNICEF Niger Country Office for a highly motivated and committed professional to serve as Deputy Representative, Operations at the P-5 level. The Deputy Representative Operations serve as a core member of the senior management team, acting as a strategic partner to the Representative and Deputy Representative Programme in ensuring the effective, efficient, and compliant management of country office. The role also strengthens internal controls, promotes a culture of accountability and service excellence, and enables evidence-based decision-making, thereby supporting the Representative in achieving organizational objectives and maximizing impact at country level. Further, the role provides leadership and oversight of the operations function – covering administration budget, finance, Digital Impact, supply chain, and risk management while aligning Operations management with Programme delivery focusing on programmatic priorities. By leading multiple cross-functional teams, the Deputy Representative Operations drives integrated planning, resource optimization, risk management and performance monitoring, ensuring that systems, processes and people are positioned to deliver results.

item.title: Programme Specialist (Financing for Scale), P-4, Fixed Term Position, #00133668, Global Programme Division, Nutrition and Child Development, Brussels, Belgium
item.description: Join UNICEF’s Global Programme Division and help advance financing solutions that improve nutrition outcomes for children, adolescents, and women. As Programme Specialist (Financing for Scale), you will provide strategic leadership and technical expertise to strengthen nutrition financing through the Child Nutrition Fund (CNF), supporting governments and UNICEF Country Offices to identify, develop, and implement financing opportunities that increase investment in nutrition. You will build partnerships with multilateral development banks, international financial institutions, and other development finance actors, while advancing innovative and catalytic financing approaches. The role also leads evidence generation, knowledge development, advocacy, and thought leadership efforts to elevate nutrition financing on global, regional, and national agendas. Through these efforts, you will help mobilize resources, strengthen country-led investments, and expand the reach and impact of the CNF in support of improved outcomes for children.
